title: Reactions may involve more than feelings
explanation: Changes can appear in different domains and at different times. Some people notice distress later; visible productivity or the absence of tears does not determine whether support is needed.
reflection: Optional reflectionWhy can someone's outward productivity tell us little about their support needs?

title: Support begins with present needs
explanation: Practical assistance and respectful choices can be offered without requesting a full account. A supporter should stay within their role and help connect with appropriate care when necessary.
reflection: Optional reflectionHow can support be offered without asking someone to relive what happened?

title: Orient to the present if comfortable
explanation: Present-focused attention offers a brief orientation to the current environment. It does not require describing an event, and stopping remains appropriate if discomfort or disconnection increases.
reflection: Optional reflectionWhy is stopping an available choice throughout the exercise?

title: Choose one accessible daily anchor
explanation: An accessible anchor can make an ordinary day more predictable. Help with transport, care responsibilities or another task may be more useful than setting a larger personal goal.
reflection: Optional reflectionWhich practical assistance could make a daily task easier?

title: Choose support that respects boundaries
explanation: A contact can be chosen for a particular kind of help without receiving a trauma history. Privacy, trust and the person’s boundaries guide what is shared and with whom.
reflection: Optional reflectionHow can a support plan respect the choice not to disclose?

title: Scenario A: Distress after a road accident
explanation: These are later difficulties following an accident, not a reenactment. Assistance with transport and assessment respects choice without forcing exposure.
reflection: Optional reflectionWhy would forcing the student to travel be an unsuitable test?

title: Scenario B: A health worker after an emergency
explanation: Continuing to work does not show that someone is unaffected. Support should be confidential and should not demand a detailed account of the emergency.
reflection: Optional reflectionWhat protects choice and privacy in the supportive conversation?

title: Scenario C: Persistent fear after repeated threats
explanation: Current threats must be considered first. Staying away from someone unsafe can be protective, and any care needs to respect privacy and protection.
reflection: Optional reflectionWhen might keeping distance be a safety measure rather than a problem to overcome?

title: Scenario D: A young person’s changed behavior
explanation: A calm private conversation can offer choice and age-appropriate support. The adult should not demand public disclosure or a complete account.
reflection: Optional reflectionHow could an adult offer support without asking the young person to explain everything?
